name: Courtscan
what: Every verdict on GenLayer, and whether it actually stands

assay.what: runs controlled consensus rounds so the point where agreement stops can be measured rather than guessed at
assay.consensus_round: probe: STRICT uses gl.vm.run_nondet_unsafe with a custom validator comparing exactly the bound fields; COMPARATIVE describes the same condition in a principle string, so the two can be compared

assay_compose.what: the third axis: rounds where validators must COMPOSE a judgement under a clock (a decision, a named precedent, a holding sentence, a rationale) rather than choose fixed fields, so the cost of generating agreement can be measured
assay_compose.consensus_round: probe_compose: always COMPARATIVE, since composed prose cannot be matched character for character; the principle asks whether two independently composed judgements mean the same thing. compose_budget 1..4 is how many composed fields must be produced and agreed
assay_compose.why_separate: the combined classify and compose source exceeds the network's per-transaction deploy gas cap (between 16M and 17M), so the compose axis is its own lean contract

the_round_that_makes_the_case.actually: result TIMEOUT, the leader's answer discarded, nothing decided
the_round_that_makes_the_case.leader_said: {"ok": true, "decision": "WARN", "precedent": "none", "holding": "An agent must not exceed its weekly budget..."}

measured.network_agreement_rate: about 99.7% over a sampled window of blocks
measured.size_axis: 12000 characters with one bound field agreed, so payload size alone did not break agreement up to the contract's ceiling
measured.correction: the project began on the belief that size was the lever, from a contract that timed out at 8000 characters. The measurement did not support it; that contract bound three fields and carried a decision history, so binding is the likelier lever and is what is being measured now
measured.binding_axis: four bound fields at 1500 characters agreed, so binding did not break it either
measured.state: the laboratory has not yet reproduced an agreement failure. Every frontier row is unbracketed and the site says so. The one real failure behind the project happened in the wild, in a contract that asked validators to compose a judgement rather than classify a document
measured.next_axis: how much the validators must generate, rather than how much they read or how many fields they must match

asymmetry: a round that agreed wrote itself into the contract and cannot be faked; a round that failed had its state change discarded, so it is attested afterwards with a transaction hash anybody can check
needs_no_wallet: looking up any round or contract
